A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we find that the infectiousness of a SARS CoV2 infected person is dependent on the age of the person and the time they spent in quarantine.
the effectiveness of various interventions can be quantified using contact tracing and sequencing data.

we find that infectiousness is highly correlated with the time spent outside of quarantine, with the working population having the highest infectiousness, and that vaccination strategies based on ascending age are more effective at reducing infections than vaccination strategies based on descending age.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effectiveness of non pharmaceutical interventions and vaccination strategies can be quantified directly by reconstructing the transmission tree.
the effectiveness of non pharmaceutical interventions is highly dependent on the behavior of the population.

the infectiousness of individuals can be quantified directly from transmission trees, and that this can be done in a way that is not confounded by changes in behavior due to non pharmaceutical interventions.
